public_reach.rationale: The occurrence's own headline event argues against listed reach: ClearSpace, the winner of the flagship UK national contract, is confirmed a private Swiss company, an EPFL Space Center spin-off, per EPFL's own account. LeoLabs and Slingshot Aerospace, the space-situational-awareness/tracking names behind the removal layer, are also private (unconfirmed as public by any source found this run, consistent with Nell's own 2026-09-01 finding). The one clean listed pure-play in the sector, Astroscale Holdings (Tokyo Stock Exchange: 186A), holds only a smaller UK contract (a GBP 1.95 million COSMIC continuation award) rather than the main national mission, so the largest single dated dollar figure in this occurrence lands on a private company, not the listed one. Scored at 30 rather than 15 because Astroscale is a real, IPO'd, exchange-listed operator actively winning government ADR work, just not the largest award found this run.

capture_odds.rationale: The sector's one listed operator is not yet converting activity into profit: Astroscale Holdings' own reporting shows project income rising 38.4% year on year while the company posted a profit before tax of negative 16,323 million yen, i.e. growing revenue and a widening loss simultaneously. That is the price-taker/pre-commercial pattern this leg's low anchor describes, not concentrated pricing power, and it sits at a company still substantially dependent on government grants and phased demonstration contracts (its own COSMIC award, GBP 1.95M, is a continuation-funding contract, not a commercial sale) rather than a market clearing price for a repeatable removal service. Scored at 22 rather than 15 because Astroscale is at least generating and growing real revenue against this exact business line, not merely a cost center.
